title: add nvtx instrumentation and microbench harness for kernel scheduling & kv-cache
author: Asha Kumar
description: Introduce lightweight NVTX range annotations, a small counter API for runtime events (kernel selection, batch formation, KV cache hits/misses), and a microbenchmark harness that exercises scheduling and continuous-batching paths. Motivation: we have sporadic tail latency spikes and opaque GPU kernel timing that make it hard to correlate scheduler decisions with kernel performance. This PR adds unobtrusive markers and counters that are enabled by default in dev builds and opt-in in production, plus a reproducible microbench that feeds the runtime synthetic workloads across sequence lengths, batch sizes, and KV cache hit ratios so we can drive dashboards and iterate on kernel/placement heuristics. Summary of changes: - runtime/instrumentation/nvtx_annotations.h/.cc: RAII helpers to push/pop NVTX ranges for model invoke, batch formation, queue wait, kernel dispatch, kv-cache lookup; includes lightweight string interning to reduce allocation overhead. - runtime/instrumentation/counters.h/.cc: atomic counters exposed via debug endpoint; counters track kernel_variant_selected, batch_formed_size_X (per-bucket), kv_cache_hit, kv_cache_miss, queue_enqueue_ms. - runtime/bench/microbench: reproducible harness with YAML workloads that vary seq_len, batch_rate, kv_hit_rate, model_variant toggles; collects per-iteration NVTX markers, counter deltas, and raw kernel timings (when CUDA profiling enabled). - integrations/bench-grafana/dashboard.json: initial Grafana panel layout for NVTX-derived timings, counter rates, and tail-latency heatmaps. - tools/dev/profiler_agent: small tool that consumes counter snapshots and NVTX timeline and emits combined flamegraphs for quick triage. Checklist: - [x] NVTX helpers implemented with minimal overhead (dev build) - [x] Counter API + debug HTTP endpoint (+ JSON) - [x] Microbench harness + sample workloads - [x] Grafana dashboard skeleton + example panels - [x] Unit tests for counter invariants and RAII push/pop - [x] Docs: perf/INSTRUMENTATION.md with usage and opt-in ENV variable Known limitations and opt-in gating: NVTX is a build-time optional dependency; when NVTX headers are absent we compile no-op macros. Counters are guarded by a runtime flag REDWOOD_PERF_INSTRUMENT=1 and limited to dev/dedicated clusters by default. The microbench is designed for deterministic workloads but does not simulate multi-tenant unpredictability. How to use: - Enable instrumentation: REDWOOD_PERF_INSTRUMENT=1 and (optional) CUDA_NVTX=1 - Run microbench: tools/run_microbench --workload workloads/schedule_small.yaml --output out/trace.json - Upload out/trace.json to bench-grafana data source or run tools/dev/profiler_agent to produce flamegraphs and counter summaries Rationale and design notes: NVTX ranges are intentionally fine-grained: batch-formation, preflight-shape, kv-lookup, kv-apply, kv-cache-hit, kernel-dispatch, kernel-copy, kernel-exec, postprocess. We interleave counters so that dashboards can show e.g. kernel_variant_selected=optimized_fused_v2 correlated with lower kernel_exec_ms but higher kernel_copy_ms (indicating memory-layout penalty). The microbench supports toggling the runtime's kernel selection policy via an env var so we can A/B different kernel pickers deterministically. Backwards compatibility and safety: all instrumentation is opt-in and has negligible overhead in production builds unless explicitly enabled. The debug endpoint rate-limits snapshots and requires an admin token. Related: Linear ENG-1245 (scheduling tail latencies), ENG-1302 (kv-cache quality metrics), PM-58 (perf dashboard request).

review_comments:
Miguel Santos: Nice encapsulation of NVTX ranges, but we need to limit string allocations in hot paths; can we use static string ids?
Asha Kumar: Switched to interned ids and added a unit test verifying no heap alloc during push/pop for common path.
Priya Patel: Minimal API looks good; please add a short example of how to correlate counters with traces in the docs.
Asha Kumar: Added docs section 'Correlating counters and NVTX traces' and sample microbench output.
Jonah Lee: CI flake on macOS build (nvtx headers absent) — pushed a small guard patch to make macros no-op when NVTX not available.
Miguel Santos: Approved after confirming unit tests and microbench outputs are stable on our benchmark hardware.
Priya Patel: Left a follow-up note to add dashboard panels for per-model heatmaps in a later PR.
release_notes: Added NVTX range helpers, runtime counters, and a reproducible microbenchmark to collect kernel scheduling and KV cache metrics. Provides Grafana dashboard skeleton and dev tooling for flamegraph synthesis. Instrumentation is opt-in via REDWOOD_PERF_INSTRUMENT.
